opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin (E032), Analyst, full-time employee, requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E032 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note listed full-time; Security DB is authoritative here). Contractors with basic training max out at read; write requires advanced training. Recommend read.
reason: Security DB (authoritative) lists E032 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. Since the employee has basic training, the maximum allowed access is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.

content.text:
Two notes conflict: HR says full-time Analyst, Security says contractor with basic training, and Security says their DB is authoritative. According to the team, Security DB is authoritative for employment type. Contractor with basic security training: read, or write if advanced training. Never admin. So max is read. Requested write, above maximum, so grant maximum = read.

Submit decision: read.
